chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha, from Aban al-Ahmar, from Ziyad ibn Abi Raja, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Say what you know, and if you do not know then say: 'Allah is more knowing.' Indeed, a man may pick out a verse from the Qur'an and fall into it (misinterpret it) a distance farther than what is between the sky and the earth.

key_terms.اللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ: Allah is more knowing (phrase used to admit ignorance)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of picking a verse out of context according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) instructs that when giving religious rulings or explanations, one should speak only from knowledge and admit ignorance when uncertain by saying 'Allah is more knowing.' He warns that selectively extracting a verse from the Qur'an without full context or knowledge leads to significant error, metaphorically described as falling a vast distance between the sky and the earth.

en.ammaar-muslim: 3. [3/-] al-Kafi: A number of our companions from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from al-Hasan b. Ali al-Washsha from Aban al-Ahmar from Ziyad b. Abi Raja from Abi Ja’far عليه السلام who said:

say what you know and if you do not know then say: “Allāh is more knowing”, a man selectively picks out a verse from the Qur’an and falls in it (misinterpreting it) a farther distance than what is between the earth and the sky.
